summary: The paper measures the 1999 single-algorithm cross-validated filter (5-fold out-of-fold logistic regression, drop disagreements, refit) on digits and breast cancer under 20% and 40% symmetric noise, with 5 seeds. It reports that dropped samples are flipped much more often than the noise rate, that the refit beats logistic regression in three of four noisy cells, and that an untuned MLP degrades much more. Clean-label cost is below test resolution.
strengths: The scope is stated plainly: the paper says the rule is not new, lists what was not run, and the abstract and discussion carry the same caveats.
The central question (are out-of-fold disagreements flipped more often than a random drop would be?) is clear and is answered directly by precision against the realized noise rate.
The method section is short and complete: input, output, three steps, cost of K+1 fits, and no hidden thresholds. A reader could reimplement it from one page.
The teaser shows the pipeline and the headline result in one figure, and Fig. 2 shows paired gains with seed dots, which makes the spread visible.
Results subsection headings state the finding, and the MLP comparison is explicitly kept from being read as 'filtering beats deep nets'.

weaknesses.issue: The text refers to table content that is not in the tables. Sec. 5.1 says Table 2 reports 'precision next to [the realized noise rate] and the lift over it', and Sec. 5.2 points to a 'loss column' in Table 2. Table 2 has neither (columns: Dropped, Precision, p, Recall, Recovered). The reader cannot check the paper's main claim (precision vs. base rate) from the table.
weaknesses.suggestion: Add columns 'Realized noise (%)', 'Lift' (precision/noise), and 'LR loss (points)' to Table 2, or rewrite the text to match the table. Drop 'Dropped' count or convert it to a percent of training set.

weaknesses.issue: Inconsistent statistical framing. The setup says 'we report no test against a fixed level', yet Table 2 reports one-sample t-tests of precision against 50%. A 50% reference is also not the right null: the stated null is the realized noise rate (20 or 40%), and 50% is below the 64.6% precision at 20% only in a way that is irrelevant to the claim. The 'p vs 50%' column therefore confuses the message.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4 'Metrics and statistics'; Table 2 caption and p column
weaknesses.suggestion: Either test precision against the per-seed realized noise rate (paired) and say so, or remove the 50% test and the contradictory sentence. State once what null each p-value tests.

weaknesses.issue: The prose is hard to follow in the results because it is vague where numbers are available, and in places contradicts itself. 'Recovers a minor share' (intro) vs 'about a fifth' (results); breast cancer 40% is called a win 'significantly in all seeds' yet 'unstable' and 'partial'; 'precision only moderately above the noise rate' is not quantified; 'a quarter to a third of dropped samples are clean' is not directly visible in the table. Readers must reconcile these themselves.
weaknesses.suggestion: Give one consistent phrasing per cell and cite the exact table column. Add a one-line per-cell summary (e.g., a small table or caption sentence: gain, p, recovered, precision lift) so the four-cell story reads at once. Replace 'minor share' with the number.

weaknesses.issue: Hedging and negation dominate the prose (abstract, Sec. 5, Sec. 6). Roughly half of the abstract is limitations ('no comparison with other filters', 'not significant', 'below resolution'), and Sec. 6 spends its second paragraph on a long list of things not run. The main insight gets lost, and the abstract is a dense single block of about 200 words.
weaknesses.suggestion: Cut the abstract to problem, rule, finding, one honest caveat. Move the list of untested items into a short limitations paragraph framed as next steps (class-dependent noise, confident learning, random-drop control).

weaknesses.issue: Teaser (Fig. 1) problems. In panel 2 the 'clean 24%' label is clipped/overlapping the bar edge. Panel 1 shows 'flipped tag' boxes that are only schematic, and the panel 3 legend says 'Filter (ours)' while the text says it is a 1999 method, not ours. The dashed 'clean-label accuracy of filter' line is a weaker reference than the logistic regression clean accuracy.
weaknesses.suggestion: Widen the bar label or move 'clean 24%' outside. Rename the method 'Out-of-fold filter' in the figure, Table 1 and caption to match the text. State in the caption how the shown digit examples were chosen.

weaknesses.issue: The tables are placed at the end of Sec. 5 as full-width floats after all the text, and Fig. 2 appears before the section's claims it supports. Table 1 caption includes interpretation ('The filter loses little on clean data and gains most...') and bolds ties inconsistently (LR and MLP bold on clean breast cancer, filter not, with no tie rule for 96.6 vs 96.7).
weaknesses.suggestion: Put Table 1 near the first results subsection, shorten captions to what is shown and how to read it, and state the bolding rule or bold only significant best.

weaknesses.issue: Notation and naming drift. The method is called 'out-of-fold filter', 'single-algorithm filter', 'out-of-fold disagreement filter' and 'Filter (ours)'. 'Recovered' is defined only in a table caption and is called 'our own definition', yet it is central. 'Realized noise rate' appears in the setup without a definition of how it differs from 20/40%. Eq. (1) is the only equation, and the sets S and D are not used again.
weaknesses.suggestion: Pick one name and use it everywhere. Define 'recovered share' and 'realized noise rate' in Sec. 4 with a formula, not in a caption.

weaknesses.issue: Odd or misplaced sentences hurt the reading: the Setup ends with an advertisement for the Scriptorium pipeline, the title ('...A Small Measurement Study') is not the catchy finding, and the intro's last paragraph before the figure repeats the abstract's results. The related work paragraphs each end with 'we do not compare against X', which repeats Sec. 6.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4 last sentence; title; Sec. 1 para 4; Sec. 2
weaknesses.suggestion: Move the tooling statement to a footnote or acknowledgment. Make the title state the finding. State non-comparisons once, in Sec. 6.

weaknesses.issue: Fig. 2 mixes two baselines with very different ranges, so the MLP bars (up to about 28 points) squash the logistic regression gaps that carry the paper's real claim. The caption does not say what the confidence level of the intervals is, and the 5-seed CIs are asymmetric in appearance.
weaknesses.suggestion: State the CI level and method in the caption. Consider showing only the logistic regression gap in the main figure, and the MLP gap in a table, or use a shared y-axis break.

questions: What is the exact null for the precision test in Table 2, and why 50% rather than the realized noise rate?
Is 'recovered share' computed per seed and then averaged, or from mean accuracies? Does it explode when the loss is small?
How does the filter's gain on breast cancer at 20% noise compare to dropping the same number of random samples?
Why is precision lower at 40% than at 20% on breast cancer but higher on digits? A sentence of explanation would help the reader.
